questions.choice_note: any 1 of 2 questions in Section A
questions.chapter: Prime Minister and Council of Ministers
concepts: President's discretion in hung Lok Sabha
Council of Ministers appointed on PM's advice
questions.question:
The Prime Minister and his Council of Ministers formulate and implement the policies which govern the country. In this context, answer the following question:
Under what circumstances can the President use his discretion to appoint the Prime Minister? On whose advice does he appoint the Council of Ministers?
questions.solution: When no single party secures an absolute majority in the Lok Sabha, the President may have some option (discretion) in appointing the Prime Minister. (Also: he appoints a PM in case of the death of an existing Prime Minister.) He appoints the Council of Ministers on the advice of the Prime Minister.

marking_points.point: President uses discretion when no single party secures an absolute majority in the Lok Sabha (or on death of an existing PM)
Council of Ministers appointed on the advice of the Prime Minister

questions.choice_note: any 1 of 2 questions in Section A
questions.chapter: Prime Minister and Council of Ministers
questions.question:
The Prime Minister and his Council of Ministers formulate and implement the policies which govern the country. In this context, answer the following question:
What is meant by the term Collective Responsibility of Ministers?
questions.solution: The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Parliament and has to resign if it loses the confidence of the Lok Sabha. Decisions taken in Cabinet meetings apply equally to all Ministers; all Ministers jointly share responsibility for the government's policies and performance.

marking_points.point: Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to Parliament / must resign if it loses the confidence of the Lok Sabha
All ministers jointly share responsibility for government policies; Cabinet decisions bind all ministers

questions.choice_note: any 1 of 2 questions in Section A
questions.chapter: Prime Minister and Council of Ministers
questions.question:
The Prime Minister and his Council of Ministers formulate and implement the policies which govern the country. In this context, answer the following question:
Name the three categories of the Council of Ministers.
questions.solution: (a) Cabinet Ministers (b) Ministers of State (c) Deputy Ministers

questions.choice_note: any 1 of 2 questions in Section A
questions.chapter: Prime Minister and Council of Ministers
concepts: PM's powers in relation to President
questions.question:
The Prime Minister and his Council of Ministers formulate and implement the policies which govern the country. In this context, answer the following question:
Mention any three powers of the Prime Minister with reference to the President.
questions.solution: Any three: (a) All authority vested in the President is exercised by the Prime Minister. (b) On the advice of the PM the President summons and prorogues Parliament and dissolves the Lok Sabha. (c) The President appoints the Council of Ministers on the advice of the PM. (d) The PM acts as the link between the President and the Council of Ministers.

marking_points.point: Any one valid power of PM with reference to the President (e.g. President acts on PM's advice in summoning/proroguing Parliament, dissolving Lok Sabha)
Any second valid power (e.g. President appoints Council of Ministers on PM's advice)
Any third valid power (e.g. PM is the link between the President and Council of Ministers; PM exercises the authority vested in the President)

questions.choice_note: any 1 of 2 questions in Section A
questions.question:
The Supreme Court is at the apex of the entire system of judiciary. In this context, answer the following question:
What is the term of the Supreme Court judge? Name the procedure through which the judge can be removed.
questions.solution: A judge of the Supreme Court holds office until he attains the age of 65 years. He can be removed through the process of impeachment.

marking_points.point: Holds office until the age of 65 years

questions.choice_note: any 1 of 2 questions in Section A
questions.question:
The Supreme Court is at the apex of the entire system of judiciary. In this context, answer the following question:
What is meant by Judicial Review?
questions.solution: The Supreme Court has the power to review laws passed by the Union or State Legislature and can declare a law 'ultra vires' or null and void if it is against the spirit of the Constitution.

marking_points.point: Power of the Supreme Court to review laws passed by Union or State legislatures
Can declare a law ultra vires/null and void if against the Constitution

questions.choice_note: any 1 of 2 questions in Section A
questions.question:
The Supreme Court is at the apex of the entire system of judiciary. In this context, answer the following question:
Explain the term Original Jurisdiction of the Supreme Court. Mention any two kinds of cases which come under this jurisdiction.
questions.solution: Original Jurisdiction means the power to hear and determine a dispute in the first instance, i.e. cases which cannot be moved by any other court. Any two: (a) Centre-State or Inter-State disputes (b) Protection of Fundamental Rights (c) Transfer of cases from lower courts (d) Interpretation of the Constitution.

marking_points.point: Original jurisdiction: power to hear and determine a dispute in the first instance

questions.choice_note: any 1 of 2 questions in Section A
questions.question:
The Supreme Court is at the apex of the entire system of judiciary. In this context, answer the following question:
Name any three writs which can be issued by the Supreme Court.
questions.solution: Any three: Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Writ of Prohibition, Writ of Certiorari, Quo-warranto.

questions.choice_note: any 2 of 3 questions in Section B
questions.question:
The First World War had a devastating effect on the world and caused unprecedented destruction. With reference to the First World War, answer the following question:
Name the signatory countries of the Triple Entente.
questions.solution: France, Russia and England (Britain).

questions.choice_note: any 2 of 3 questions in Section B
questions.question:
The First World War had a devastating effect on the world and caused unprecedented destruction. With reference to the First World War, answer the following question:
What is meant by the term Imperialism?
questions.solution: A system by which a powerful nation used to establish its control over another country, either by political pressure, infiltration and annexation or by outright wars. Once conquered, this country was claimed as a colony.

marking_points.point: Powerful nation establishes control over another country
By political pressure, infiltration, annexation or war; the country becomes a colony

questions.choice_note: any 2 of 3 questions in Section B
concepts: Sarajevo assassination as immediate cause of WWI
questions.question:
The First World War had a devastating effect on the world and caused unprecedented destruction. With reference to the First World War, answer the following question:
Explain the immediate cause of the First World War.
questions.solution: Sarajevo Crisis (immediate cause): (a) Archduke Francis Ferdinand, heir to the throne of Austria-Hungary, was assassinated at Sarajevo. (b) The assassination was organized by a secret society called 'Black Hand' or Union of Death formed by extremists of Serbia. (c) Their main aim was to unite all Serbians into a single Serbian state. (d) Austria served an ultimatum on Serbia on July 23. (e) Serbia accepted most demands except those that would have led to loss of her sovereignty. (f) Austria declared war on Serbia on July 28, 1914.

marking_points.point: Assassination of Archduke Francis Ferdinand at Sarajevo
Organized by the Black Hand / Union of Death, Serbian extremists
Aim: unite all Serbians into a single Serbian state
Austria served an ultimatum on Serbia on July 23
Serbia accepted most demands except those threatening her sovereignty
Austria declared war on Serbia on July 28, 1914

questions.choice_note: any 2 of 3 questions in Section B
questions.topic: Treaty of Versailles reparation, military terms
concepts: War reparation 6.6 billion pounds/33 billion dollars
Military clauses of Treaty of Versailles
questions.question:
The First World War had a devastating effect on the world and caused unprecedented destruction. With reference to the First World War, answer the following question:
What was the amount of war reparation that Germany had to pay the allies? Mention any two terms of the Treaty of Versailles which affected the German military.
questions.solution: Germany had to pay for the loss and damages suffered by the Allies; reparation was fixed at 33 billion dollars. Any two military terms: (a) German army restricted to 100,000 men (b) General Staff eliminated (c) manufacture of submarines, armoured cars, tanks and fighter planes prohibited (d) navy limited to 15,000 men and 36 warships.

questions.choice_note: any 2 of 3 questions in Section B
concepts: Common ideologies of Nazism and Fascism
questions.question:
Look at the picture given and answer the questions that follow:
State any two similar ideologies of the dictators.
questions.solution: Ideologies of Nazism and Fascism, any two: (a) faith in totalitarian rule (b) despise democratic political systems (c) the state is supreme and can suppress fundamental rights and freedom of individuals (d) One-Party and One Leader (e) aggressive nationalism and imperialism (f) war as an instrument for furthering national interest (g) intensely nationalistic, anti-communist, anti-democratic rule.

questions.choice_note: any 2 of 3 questions in Section B
concepts: Invasion of Poland as immediate cause of WWII
questions.question:
Look at the picture given and answer the questions that follow:
What was the immediate cause of the Second World War? Mention any two reasons for it.
questions.solution: Immediate cause: Hitler's invasion of Poland on September 1, 1939. Any two reasons: (a) By the Treaty of Versailles Germany was divided into two parts to give a land route (Danzig/Polish Corridor) to Poland; Germany wanted to regain lost territories. (b) The city was mainly inhabited by Germans, and by occupying the Danzig Corridor Germany could connect with East Prussia. (c) Germany signed a Non-Aggression Pact with Russia in August 1939; Poland was accused of atrocities against Germans living there. (d) On September 1, 1939, German armies marched into Poland.

marking_points.point: Immediate cause: Hitler's invasion of Poland (1 September 1939)

questions.choice_note: any 2 of 3 questions in Section B
concepts: League of Nations failure and appeasement
questions.question:
Look at the picture given and answer the questions that follow:
Explain how the Japanese invasion of China became a cause for the Second World War.
questions.solution: (a) Japan's ambitions rose after the First World War; it intervened in Manchuria and, despite the League's opposition, occupied it and set up a government there. (b) Japan started an undeclared war against China in 1931. (c) China appealed to the League of Nations to declare sanctions against Japan. (d) Britain and France, leading League members, paid no attention. (e) Japan left the League of Nations and joined the Berlin-Rome-Tokyo axis. (f) Britain and France followed appeasement, so war became inevitable.

marking_points.point: Japan occupied Manchuria despite League opposition and set up a government
China appealed to the League for sanctions against Japan
Britain and France paid no attention
Japan left the League and joined the Berlin-Rome-Tokyo axis
Policy of appeasement made war inevitable

questions.choice_note: any 2 of 3 questions in Section B
questions.question:
With reference to the United Nations Organisation, answer the following question:
State any two objectives of the United Nations Organisation.
questions.solution: Any two: (a) to maintain international peace and security (b) to solve international problems of social, economic, cultural and humanitarian character (c) to promote respect for human rights (d) to employ international machinery for the promotion and advancement of all people.

questions.choice_note: any 2 of 3 questions in Section B
concepts: ICJ composition and term of judges
questions.question:
With reference to the United Nations Organisation, answer the following question:
How many judges is the International Court of Justice composed of? What is their term?
questions.solution: It consists of 15 judges elected by the General Assembly and the Security Council for a term of 9 years.

questions.choice_note: any 2 of 3 questions in Section B
questions.question:
With reference to the United Nations Organisation, answer the following question:
Mention any three functions of the General Assembly.
questions.solution: Any three: (a) consider and make recommendations on principles of cooperation in maintaining international peace and security (b) discuss any question relating to international peace and security (c) discuss and make recommendations on any question within the scope of the Charter or affecting powers and functions of any UN organ (d) initiate studies and make recommendations to promote international political, social and economic cooperation (e) make recommendations for peaceful settlement of disputes (f) receive and consider reports from the Security Council and other organs (g) elect the non-permanent members of the Security Council and the Trusteeship Council, and elect the judges of the ICJ.

questions.choice_note: any 2 of 3 questions in Section B
questions.question:
With reference to the United Nations Organisation, answer the following question:
What is the full form of WHO? Mention any two of its functions.
questions.solution: World Health Organisation. Any two functions: (a) helps countries improve health systems by building infrastructure, manpower, institutions (b) gives important drugs for medical care (c) promotes research to cure and prevent diseases (d) works towards safe drinking water and adequate waste disposal (e) organizes conferences, seminars and training for health personnel (f) fights diseases and prevents their spread (g) defines standards for strength and purity of medicines including biological products (h) publishes health journals such as the Bulletin of the World Health Organisation.
